"Hatzic" on this page is THREE governments under one board label - Hatzic Bench = City of Mission (Ferguson Avenue, Jasper Avenue, McEwen Avenue, Ferndale Avenue, Dewdney Trunk Road) — City bylaws, zoning and taxes apply, including the City's flat 10% tax penalty after July 2. - Hatzic Prairie = FVRD Electoral Area F — FVRD and Province rules, rural taxes paid to the Province (5% after July 2 + further 5% after October 31). - Hatzic Island = FVRD Electoral Area G (Shook Road addresses around Hatzic Lake and Hatzic Island) — FVRD and Province rules, rural taxes, NOT City bylaws and NOT Mission's flat 10%. The FVRD's Electoral Areas Housing Needs Report lists "Electoral Area F: McConnell Creek, Hatzic Prairie" and "Electoral Area G: Nicomen Island, Deroche, Dewdney, Hatzic Island," and states the Hatzic Valley includes the historic settlement areas of Hatzic Prairie, Durieu, Miracle Valley and McConnell Creek. All of it carries "Mission" mailing addresses and sits in the board's Hatzic sub-area — a reporting grouping only. The tax regime follows the jurisdiction the parcel sits in, not the mailing address. Which side of the City/FVRD line a specific Hatzic address sits on is UNVERIFIED at parcel level in this research — check the PID before quoting City or rural rules for a listing.

items.t: The page headed "Hatzic Lake Real Estate: Homes, Lots & Acreages" showed 55 results at reading — a snapshot, not a market statistic. Every first-page card is labelled board sub-area "Hatzic" with a "Mission" mailing address, but the streets split into two different worlds: Bench streets inside the city (Ferguson Avenue, Jasper Avenue, McEwen Avenue, Ferndale Avenue, Dewdney Trunk Road) and Shook Road addresses around Hatzic Lake and Hatzic Island.
FVRD Prairie and Island ground has no SnapStats coverage of its own — no figure is quoted for it.

City planning frame (Bench only): the City of Mission's Official Community Plan is Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted April 21, 2026, replacing Bylaw 6350-2025 with the same vision, land use framework, mapping and policy direction, with a Regional Context Statement added. This City frame does not govern the FVRD parts of the page; FVRD official community plan and zoning bylaws govern Areas F and G, with the specific bylaw numbers and zone names for a given Prairie/Island lot to be confirmed with the FVRD for the PID.

items.t: Secondary suites, two frames on one page: inside the City (Bench only), all secondary suites must be registered with the City, a suite is a self-contained living space in a single family home forming part of the same real estate entity, and suites are not permitted in townhouses or rowhomes. In FVRD Electoral Area F (Prairie), secondary suites are freely permitted with no restrictions related to farm use, but must be located within the principal dwelling and could not be a separate detached structure such as a garden suite. Which frame applies depends on which side of the City/FVRD line the parcel sits on.

ALR housing and stratification rules: the majority of the inhabited Hatzic Valley is in the ALR. On ALR parcels the housing frame is one principal residence at a maximum of 500 m² plus at most one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha), and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; a strata plan deposit is a subdivision — Strata Property Act s. 239; ALR subdivision needs Commission permission — Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)). Whether a specific Hatzic parcel is in the ALR: UNVERIFIED at parcel level.

items.t: The mailing address lies about who governs you — on two-thirds of this page. Every listing here carries a Mission mailing address, yet a Ferguson Avenue house pays City taxes under City bylaws while a Shook Road property on Hatzic Island or in Hatzic Prairie is FVRD/Province ground with rural taxes (due July 2; 5% after July 2 and a further 5% after October 31). A buyer who budgets Mission's flat 10% for a Prairie or Island parcel has the wrong regime — and vice versa.

Three tenures sit within one feed page at overlapping prices. A fee-simple Bench house, an Everglades undivided-interest seasonal lot and a Green Acres pad home are three different assets with different financing, seasonal-use and resale structures — tenure, park/resort rules and any seasonal-use limit must come from the park's or resort's own documents, not the listing card.

The one verified 55+ product here comes with an unsettled tax line. Mission Mobile Home Park's listings state 55+ outright, but its parcel-level City/FVRD jurisdiction is UNVERIFIED in this research — confirm the parcel's tax regime, its flood status and the pad tenancy terms together, not separately.
Zero attached listings is itself the market fact.

items.t: One page, three governments, two tax calendars. A Ferguson Avenue house pays City taxes with a flat 10% penalty after July 2; a Shook Road property on the Island or in the Prairie pays the Province at 5% + 5% (July 2 / October 31). Budgeting either regime for the other ground is simply wrong — and Mission MHP's own side is UNVERIFIED, so its homes take no quoted regime until the PID is checked.

The cheapest "land" on the page is not land. Everglades use-areas and Green Acres pads sit in the same $229,000–$415,000 card range as real product on the first page, but they are a seasonal undivided interest and a pad tenancy — different financing, seasonal-use and resale structures from a fee-simple Bench lot.
The Mission OCP date matters and is often misstated.

Suites run on two different rulebooks on one page. City suites must be registered and are barred in townhouses/rowhomes; Area F suites must sit inside the principal dwelling with no detached garden-suite route. The PID's side of the line decides which book applies.

The West Coast Express does not serve the lake. It runs from Mission City Station in the City (five weekday westbound trains, 75 minutes to Waterfront, no weekend service); no transit summary for the lake, Island or Prairie was opened — drive times from the lake are UNVERIFIED.

faq.a: Partly. The Hatzic Bench is inside the City of Mission, but Hatzic Prairie is Fraser Valley Regional District Electoral Area F and Hatzic Island is Electoral Area G — the FVRD's housing-needs report lists Area F as "McConnell Creek, Hatzic Prairie" and Area G as "Nicomen Island, Deroche, Dewdney, Hatzic Island" — and all of it carries Mission mailing addresses and sits in the board's Hatzic sub-area.

faq.q: How did Hatzic sell in September 2026?
faq.a: Detached recorded 20 listings with 3 sold (a 15% sales ratio, the second-highest published detached ratio in Mission that month, on a small count of 3 sales), and Condos & Townhomes recorded 0 listings and 0 sold, so no attached ratio exists; no sub-area median is published for Hatzic, and the Mission community medians (detached $814,000; attached $430,000) are board context, not Hatzic figures (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Who do I pay property tax to on a Hatzic property?
faq.a: It depends on which Hatzic: Bench properties inside the City of Mission pay the City (2026 taxes due July 2, 2026, 10% penalty July 3); Hatzic Prairie and Hatzic Island properties are rural — their owners receive the notice from the Province's Surveyor of Taxes Office and pay the Province, with rural taxes due July 2 and 5% + 5% penalties under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Hatzic?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 20 houses listed with 3 sold in the month in Hatzic. Those are month-end counts and move daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Hatzic a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In September 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 15%, a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: Are there any condos in Hatzic?
faq.a: None verified — no condo building on the Bench, the Prairie or the Island was confirmed on an official, developer or strata source, no townhome complex was confirmed, and the board counted 0 Condos & Townhomes listings in the Hatzic sub-area in September 2026. A buyer who wants a Mission condo is buying in the core Mission sub-area, documented in the city condo notes.

faq.q: Who do I pay property tax to on a Hatzic property, and what is the penalty?
faq.a: It depends on which Hatzic: Bench properties inside the City of Mission pay the City (2026 taxes due July 2, 2026, flat 10% penalty July 3); Hatzic Prairie and Hatzic Island properties are rural — their owners receive the notice from the Province's Surveyor of Taxes Office and pay the Province, with rural taxes due July 2 and 5% + 5% penalties under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act. The regime follows the jurisdiction, not the mailing address — confirm the PID first, including for a home at Mission Mobile Home Park, whose parcel-level line is UNVERIFIED in this research.

faq.q: What am I buying at Everglades Resort?
faq.a: A seasonal recreational interest, not a home lot: fresh records show Type Recreational / Land, "No year round living," and Title to Land: Undivided Interest on a unit record. Financing, resale, use windows and fees run through the resort's own documents — read them before comparing its price to a Bench house or a park home.

faq.q: If I buy at Mission Mobile Home Park or Green Acres, what do I own?
faq.a: The manufactured home — not the pad. Pad tenancies are under the MHPTA province-wide: pad-rent increases once in 12 months on three full months' notice, capped at 2.3% plus the proportional amount for 2026 (2.2% for 2027), and a sale needs the landlord's assignment consent under s. 28. Mission Mobile Home Park's 55+ is a park rule, not a strata bylaw; Green Acres states park approval required and no age rule in any listing checked (UNCONFIRMED).

faq.q: Is an Everglades Resort lot a cheap way to own at Hatzic Lake?
faq.a: Confirm what interest actually transfers before writing.

The valley has a documented history — the 1948 dyke break put Hatzic Prairie largely under water — but a specific property's flood status and dyke protection are parcel-specific and UNVERIFIED in this research.

faq.q: Who do I pay property tax to?
faq.a: It depends on which Hatzic: Bench properties pay the City (2026 taxes due July 2, 2026, flat 10% penalty July 3); Prairie and Island properties are rural — notice from the Surveyor of Taxes Office, pay the Province, due July 2 with 5% + 5% penalties. Confirm the PID's jurisdiction first — including for a home at Mission Mobile Home Park, whose parcel-level line is UNVERIFIED.

faq.q: Is an Everglades "lot" a lot I own?
faq.a: No — Everglades Resort holdings are an undivided-interest seasonal use holding ("No year round living" in the listing records), not a fee-simple lot and not a strata lot. Confirm what interest transfers from the resort's own documents before writing.
